hints: Count the DNA bases. You have 12 bases, so that will make 4 codons. Remember this DNA section is transcribed, so you cannot read it directly from the table, you must first make the complementary mRNA.
Pair up the DNA template with mRNA using complementary base pairing (G with C, C with G). Then split your mRNA into groups of three and match each codon to the table.
walkthrough:
**Spot that this is the template strand**

This DNA sequence is transcribed, so it acts as the template for making mRNA. That means the mRNA will be complementary to it, not identical to it.

Remember the pairing for transcription:
$$DNA\ G \rightarrow mRNA\ C, \quad DNA\ C \rightarrow mRNA\ G$$

**Transcribe DNA to mRNA**

Write the complementary mRNA underneath the DNA, then split into threes.

DNA: GCG CGC GGC GCG
mRNA: CGC GCG CCG CGC

So your four mRNA codons are CGC, GCG, CCG, CGC.

**Translate using the table**

Now just look up each mRNA codon in the table. CGC = Arg, GCG = Ala, CCG = Pro, CGC = Arg.

That gives the order:
$$Arg-Ala-Pro-Arg$$

options.A: Incorrect. Ala-Ala-Cys-Ala does not match any of the mRNA codons made from this template. Cys (UGC) in particular cannot be made as there is no A in the DNA.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the common trap of reading the DNA directly as if it were mRNA (GCG = Ala). You must first make the complementary mRNA from the template strand.
options.C: Correct. The complementary mRNA is CGC-GCG-CCG-CGC, which translates to Arg-Ala-Pro-Arg using the table.
options.D: Incorrect. Thr is coded by ACG, which is not present in the correct mRNA sequence CGC-GCG-CCG-CGC.
